plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated interaction to exploit, the safest and most profit-maximizing action is to bid exactly my private value of $20.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down - bidding above value risks winning at a loss, and bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit in this single-round game.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $40 to maximize expected profit.
